column1: # What each source revision the Dockerfile clones is meant to follow, and why.
# A pin listed here is watched by scripts/check-upstream-pins.sh. A pin the
# Dockerfile clones but this file does not name is a failure, so adding a source
# to the image forces a ruling instead of leaving it unwatched.
# Columns, tab separated: owner/repo, policy, reason.
# release-tag     the revision has to be the newest semver tag of that repo.
#                 These are installed with luarocks make, so a tagged release is
#                 what upstream treats as consumable, and a commit landing on the
#                 default branch past that tag is not staleness. The check does
#                 not report it, which is what keeps this from reporting twelve
#                 pins as behind on every run.
# default-branch  the revision has to be the tip of the default branch.
# The reason column says what the pin provides, so a later reader can tell which
# rendering stops working if the pin is dropped.
Omikhleia/resilient.sile
column3: The document classes the renderer targets. Upstream tags releases again (v4.2.0, v4.2.1), so the image follows the newest tag like the libraries and addons; main past v4.2.1 adds packages its tagged 4.2.x rockspecs do not list.
